results: pdftotext 24.02.0 runs correctly from the isolated extracted-.deb location with no system-wide install.

Multi-column synthetic PDF, plain mode: output alternates LEFTCOL-ALPHA, RIGHTCOL-ECHO, LEFTCOL-BETA, RIGHTCOL-FOXTROT, ... i.e. it interleaves by visual row rather than reading column 1 top-to-bottom then column 2 -- NOT true column-major logical reading order for independent columns. -layout mode instead prints each row's left+right fragments concatenated on one physical line ('LEFTCOL-ALPHA one two three       RIGHTCOL-ECHO thirteen fourteen'), which is also not column-major order. Neither mode reconstructs the intended per-column reading order without added heuristics.

Scanned (image-only) PDF: pdftotext -layout produced a 1-byte output file (effectively empty; only a form-feed). Confirms Poppler's pdftotext performs no OCR and extracts zero usable text from a scanned page, exactly as the gap predicted.

Public annual-report PDF (Berkshire Hathaway 2022 shareholder letter, born-digital): body paragraph extraction is correct and phrase-exact -- 'Warren E. Buffett' (signature line) and 'Charlie Munger, my long-time partner, and I have the job of managing the savings of' both found verbatim via grep on the -layout output. The first-page performance table (which uses dot-leader formatting, not a simple grid) extracts with all data present but with very large runs of literal '.' characters and wide whitespace gaps between the year and the two percentage columns -- readable by a human but not directly machine-parseable as clean cells without additional dot-leader-aware post-processing.
limits: Poppler version differs from the Mac-qualified 26.09.0 (this Linux host used the Ubuntu-24.04-repo build 24.02.0, obtained via `apt-get download` + local dpkg-deb extraction into the isolated cache dir, never installed system-wide); results are illustrative of the same upstream project's known OCR/layout limitations, not a same-version replay of the Mac acceptance run.

The 'scanned PDF' fixture is a synthetic image-wrap of an existing born-digital PDF page rather than a real scanner output (no scanner noise, skew, or DPI variance); this is a reasonable proxy for 'has no text layer' but not a full scanned-document corpus.

The multi-column test used one small 2-column synthetic layout, not a real multi-column magazine/journal page; it demonstrates the reading-order problem exists but does not quantify it across varied real layouts.

The annual-report arm covers one public PDF (Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter) and one table; it establishes that paragraph extraction is reliable and dot-leader tables are messy but present, without exhaustively scoring every page or answering semantic questions -- semantic-question qualification remains untested here.
